title: Welcome to Laundry Service
excerpt: A first look at the perfectly ordinary laundromat hiding some very unusual ambitions.
body: EDITOR NOTE: This is a suggested first devlog draft. Review and edit it before publishing.
Welcome to Laundry Service, a comedic management game about running a neighborhood laundromat while secretly building an evil lair in the back room.

The everyday work matters: customers need working washers and dryers, drop-off orders have deadlines, and the bills still need to be paid. Meanwhile, behind the scenes, you'll research peculiar equipment, meet a cast of recurring characters, and discover increasingly elaborate Operations.
I'm building Laundry Service in GameMaker. This development log will be where I share new features, screenshots, design decisions, and the occasional unexpected disaster. Thanks for following along!

title: The First Loads and a Very Suspicious Back Room
excerpt: The first playable week brought washing, drying, drop-off orders, business finances, Ronny, and the beginnings of the evil lair.
body: Week 1: September 25–October 1, 2026. This was the first documented week of playable development. I built the laundromat's basic management loop and started connecting an ordinary laundry business to the much less ordinary operation behind it.

The first version let players buy and place washers, welcome customers, run wash cycles, and collect the earnings. I added a 64×64 placement grid, valid and blocked placement previews, overlap protection, refunds for canceled purchases, camera movement, and zoom. Machines gained coin storage, collection indicators, and right-click actions for moving, selling, and repairing. The starting 5×5 floor could be expanded to 10×8, and a folding table became the first decorative furniture item.

Dryers turned that prototype into a washing-and-drying workflow. Customers could bring one to three loads, pay for each completed machine cycle, and show what they needed through status bubbles. I also added the Laundry Service counter: customers could drop off bags, leave while their orders were processed, and return to collect them. Whether an order was ready on time affected the payment. Machine locks let the player reserve equipment for these hands-on orders while keeping self-service customers away.

I added the daily business structure: an 8:00 AM–6:00 PM clock, opening and closing, customer cleanup after closing, end-of-day results, and a Next Day transition. Pause, play, fast-forward, and later dedicated 2× controls made the simulation easier to manage. The first HUD and sliding menu exposed money, happiness, cleanliness, shopping, metrics, and options. Hover information explained customers' needs and the state of their bags, while collection, breakdown, and repair sounds gave actions more feedback.

Maintenance became part of running the business. Customers could spill things, cleanliness could deteriorate, and washers, dryers, and service counters could break. Repairs consumed tools, and customer happiness responded to successful visits, impatience, and abandonment. The first balance pass set basic washers and dryers to $500, starting money to $5,000, starting tools to 20, breakdown chances to 2%, and repairs to five tools. I also revised spill cleanup so cleaning restored the cleanliness loss that had accumulated.

I introduced ways to occupy waiting customers and earn extra income. The Arcade Cabinet added paid plays and a pause in customer impatience. The Slot Machine introduced wagers, jackpots, losing streaks, and stored earnings. A three-seat Waiting Bench helped customers remain patient while looking for available machines. I improved appliance approach positions, reservations, bag pickup, and pathfinding so tightly arranged equipment was more usable.

The evil lair received its own visible floor and music transition, and Ronny introduced the criminal-business side. His first laundry visit led to dialogue, a contact unlock, and a later explanation of money jobs. The Money Washer processed disguised cash bags for a percentage of their value. A Safe offered the tempting alternative of taking the entire bag and failing the job. Suspicion, failed-job approval losses, theft of exposed processed cash, and separate art for laundry bags, disguised deliveries, and revealed money established the first consequences.

The Realtor introduction gave the player a name and title, along with a $10,000 mortgage. I added $500 weekly payments, grace periods, overdue tracking, and extra payments. The Notepad tracked known obligations, while expanded financial reports separated revenue, tool spending, slot payouts, and net operating profit. A fade-to-black transition connected the business days.

I finished the week with a title screen offering New Game, four-slot loading, and Exit, plus windowed and fullscreen display options. Placement became more precise: physical footprints were separated from transparent sprite padding, obstruction messages and footprint outlines explained blocked positions, and snapping options gave players more control. Washers, dryers, and slot machines gained saved facing directions and direction-specific access points. The exterior entrance became movable, and depth sorting made appliances overlap according to their position.

title: Research, Aliens, and a Little Brainwashing
excerpt: The lair gained research and Operations, alien customers arrived, and poor cleanliness and criminal activity began carrying serious consequences.
body: Week 2: October 2–8, 2026. I expanded the game beyond the first business loop with a tutorial, research progression, villainous Operations, and the first connections between world domination and the everyday laundromat.

I extended directional artwork and rotation across washers, dryers, Money Washers, Arcades, folding tables, and Laundry Service counters. Players could rotate supported objects with R while buying or moving them. Counter bag positions, pickup areas, and customer access points rotated with the furniture. Stable bottom anchors stopped different views from jumping vertically, and a no-path warning made unreachable machines, counters, and exits easier to identify.

The first optional Day 1 journal tutorial provided six guided lessons with animated arrows. Players could drag the journal, and its position and progress were saved. I added the Research Bench, later renamed Research Desk, with timed projects, prerequisites, progress bars, and completion audio support. That early layout grew into a larger technology chart with a separate Schemes system. Unfinished research was marked Coming soon, while locked shop products were hidden until their research was complete.

The alien Operation introduced a longer chain of objectives: discover a scheme, keep or discard it, build a Communicator, complete the transmission minigame, make contact, research a Portal Receiver, and open the way for alien laundry traffic. The Communicator and receiver gained their own equipment states, and alien customers joined the simulation. I also added a movable doorway between the laundromat and lair, with routing rules that kept ordinary customers out of the back room.

Ronny's relationship system became much more substantial. Successful and failed jobs changed approval, missing money became debt, and repayment or recovery favors offered ways to improve the situation. Negative relationships could lead to extortion, theft, sabotage, and eventually a Ronny game-over ending. Laundry Service also became a starting unlock, although its counter still had to be purchased, and completed orders left collectible cash on the counter.

Cleanliness gained direct business and legal consequences. Dirty conditions reduced incoming customer waves, and spills could cause customers to fall. A short rescue window gave the player a chance to help and reduce the chance of a lawsuit. Lawsuits were settled in the daily financial report, and a negative cash balance after settlement could cause bankruptcy. Falls, rescue timing, and lawsuit threats made a neglected floor matter beyond the cleanliness number.

The Player Brain became a physical presence in the lair, including the ability to put it through washers and dryers. World Domination began at 10%, and completing one of those cycles reduced it. I reorganized the HUD around World Domination, Suspicion, and tools. Operation Brain Wash introduced separate research requirements for the Hypno Wash 3000 and Brain Washer, brainwashing progress, domination rewards, and suspicion consequences when hypnosis went wrong.

Suspicion began attracting law enforcement. I added escalating warnings, police and LBI visits, fines, raids, confiscation, and arrest, with dedicated police and detective visuals. Officials could witness exposed criminal transactions, connecting what happened on the floor to the larger risk system. I also added service-order cycle timers, improved bag and icon layering, extended breakdowns to Arcades and Slot Machines, and corrected research and scheme-unlock behavior.

Supporting work included persistent customer appearance variation, better character depth sorting, Escape-to-open-menu behavior, and a larger developer menu for testing money, tools, research, faction approval, suspicion, and equipment. These tools made the growing number of progression paths easier to inspect during development.

title: Expeditions, Three Wishes, and My First Henchmen
excerpt: Anthony Bones brought mystery packages, the Genie brought questionable opportunities, and Doyle and Carnegie made the business less lonely.
body: Week 3: October 9–15, 2026. This week added several of the game's major characters and production systems. Expeditions, magical wishes, recruitable help, chemistry, and retail sales started turning the laundromat into a much stranger small business.

I made failure states clearer and more consistent. The mortgage now moved through a due date, grace period, final notice, and foreclosure. Bankruptcy, foreclosure, arrest, and Ronny's ending gained fade-to-black presentation and explanations of what happened. Signed HUD popups showed changes to happiness, cleanliness, domination, suspicion, and tools. The Notepad gained likely-lawsuit totals, and depositing criminal money into a Safe increased Suspicion.

Anthony Bones became a recurring customer whose successful visits could lead to an expedition through the Jungle, Ocean, and Desert. Postal Worker deliveries brought paid mystery packages every five to seven days after his adventure began. Those packages could contain postcards, weighted rewards, unique artifacts, decorations, valuables, or junk. I then made them sealed, placeable objects so their contents stayed hidden until opened, giving deliveries a physical place in the laundromat.

The Genie Lamp introduced Operation: Three Wishes. Rubbing the lamp brought a wandering Genie and a menu with confirmation, unique choices, and a strict three-wish limit. The first implemented effects covered wealth, customer traffic, mortgage changes, machine behavior, fame, gold, faction relationships, suspicion, and research. Wishes were irreversible, and using the third one left an Empty Genie Lamp trophy. The wider menu still contained choices that would need later implementation.

Doyle arrived as the first recruitable worker, with a Day 2 introduction, dialogue, a portrait, and a saved recruitment decision. He could help with Laundry Service, repairs, spill cleaning, and collecting earnings. I added enabled and disabled duties, reorderable priorities, and safeguards against tasks being ignored indefinitely. His work needed pathfinding, reservations, bag carrying, dragging, interruption handling, and recovery when a task became stuck.

Operation: Musclehead connected Doyle to the Chemist Station, numbered compounds, recipes, a Refrigerator, a Training Dummy, and Serum progression. Enhanced Doyle gained faster movement and work, but the Operation's outcome gave his new strength a pacifist twist. I also improved his duty selection and collection rules, reduced his normal walking speed, and preserved the enhanced movement bonus.

Chemistry developed into its own production loop. The station combined three numbered compounds, including the household recipes 404 Bleach, 123 Softener, and 321 Detergent. Players could buy compounds in quantities, store them in a Refrigerator, experiment with combinations, and deal with failed mixtures or spills from discarded ingredients. I balanced compound and product prices and added four-item product cases for restocking.

The Storefront turned crafted cleaning products into another source of business income. Players could stock products, attract shoppers, complete sales, and track inventory and customer reservations. A researched Change Machine added player deposits, staged customer use, completion tracking, and collection of the cycled deposit. I fixed reservation handling across the Change Machine, Pinball, Soda Machine, and Snack Machine.

The research catalogue grew with the faster Turbo Washer and Turbo Dryer, plus Pinball, Soda, and Snack Machines. Vending introduced limited stock, refill packs, earnings, customer patience effects, and litter. Equipment gained lock-status icons, and I improved their positioning, layering, footprints, and context-menu checks. Dialogue portraits also received clipping and framing fixes.

The Genie wish Give Doyle a brother introduced Carnegie. He inherited the worker system while bringing slower movement, his own priorities, and periods of confusion. Save work also expanded substantially: I improved validation, migrations, backup and temporary-save recovery, queued saves around night transitions, and clearer error messages. Dedicated Communicator and Portal Receiver screens and corrected Brain Wash quadrant ordering rounded out the week's interface work.

title: Bigger Machines and a Laundromat That Comes to Life
excerpt: Mega machines, animated appliances and characters, new walls, and a redesigned HUD brought the game closer to its visual identity.
body: Week 4: October 16–22, 2026. A fifteen-day playthrough led to a broad round of fixes, and I spent much of the week making the game easier to understand and more expressive on screen. This included larger-capacity machines, more useful help, animated equipment, and a shared animation system for the cast.

I separated everyday chemistry and retail from Operation Musclehead. The Chemist Station, Storefront, product cases, and household recipes became available independently, while Musclehead continued to gate the special Serum and Training Dummy. The special formula became Serum 789, with its own artwork, rarity-based compound pricing, Refrigerator storage and retrieval, and safe disposal on the floor.

Several playthrough issues received direct fixes. Named characters gained a right-click Talk action, players could take a Laundry Service bag from a henchman's hands, and Storefront inventory became visible through hover text. Shoppers could wander after buying. I corrected the Change Machine's failure to attract use and fixed the Communicator and Portal Receiver destination dropdowns.

The Mega Washer and Mega Dryer introduced two-load cycles, with their own research blueprints. Their behavior was integrated with earnings, placement, saves, spills, and breakdowns. Follow-up work corrected their footprints, sprite origins, customer approach points, reservations, retreat paths, and animation triggers. Turbo Washer placement also received an alignment correction.

I reorganized the Laundry and Lair shops into clearer categories and paired washer and dryer research into a more readable layout. Long labels and research cards gained better scaling and wrapping. The HUD received a larger resource display, a centered day-and-time plaque, a hanging Open/Closed sign, and styled speed controls. Later in the week, resource labels became icons with values and hover explanations.

Standard, Turbo, and Mega appliances gained idle, running, finished, and broken artwork. The Standard Washer also gained static side and back views while retaining its animated front states. Customers learned to step a short, reachable distance away from running machines, keeping the animation visible without losing their reservation or interrupting the cycle. I also repaired sprite references and save-loading crashes caused by renamed appliance resources.

Doyle gained directional walking, followed by an animated customer pool with consistent walking, idle facing, and appliance-facing behavior. I established a shared 64×64, 28-frame animation layout and validation for incomplete sheets. The same framework expanded to the Detective, Kim, Carnegie, Ronny, police, mobsters, Anthony, aliens, and the Postal Worker. Direction mappings, origins, gliding, and rapid direction changes all received attention, and customer appearance remained stable across saves.

The rooms gained expanding back walls, outside side walls, and a shared divider while preserving the doorway between them. Placement clearance was updated around those walls. I removed the old floating EVIL LAIR label and kept the actual floor grid and room geometry aligned. Holding Shift temporarily disabled attraction to nearby furniture during placement while retaining the underlying grid.

Machine feedback became more compact. Repair, collection, full-coin, active-laundry, and finished-laundry indicators moved into smaller badges, with improved ordering between cash, locks, wrenches, bags, and emotes. I added animated hypnosis, impatience, washing, drying, and no-path emotes, revised lock artwork, and connected animated Serum Doyle art while preserving his bonuses. Police and LBI dialogue modes, names, and portraits were corrected as well.

The Day 1 journal was revised repeatedly, with ongoing objectives moved to the Notepad. Tracking covered research, Anthony, Doyle, mortgage obligations, Suspicion, Ronny, lawsuits, and detective warnings. Examine and Help windows explained equipment and systems. The tutorial grew to require two washers and two dryers, show purchase progress, separate cash and coin collection, and give closing its own final step. Anthony's tutorial visit was fixed so it continued into ordinary laundry and counted toward his story.

I also produced separate visual assets: brain-in-a-jar sprite experiments at three sizes and a 3840×2160 top-down city background. These were completed artwork deliverables; the city background was documented as not yet imported into GameMaker that week. Larger dialogue panels and a dedicated row for responses helped the in-game presentation move forward alongside that art work.

title: A Phone, a Community, and a Paper Trail
excerpt: Daily events, customer personalities, community donations, advertising, and a cellphone interface made each business day more involved.
body: Week 5: October 23–29, 2026. I focused on making the laundromat feel like part of a town. Customers gained more individual behavior, daily events created new decisions, Ronny's requests became a reusable system, and the phone began bringing the game's growing set of menus together.

I continued improving the opening experience. The tutorial received speed-control guidance, a clearer final Open/Closed prompt, and an immediate customer wave after completion. I added 2.5× speed, reordered appliance actions, enabled direct vending-machine restocking, and fixed right-click menus across furniture, machines, spills, packages, supplies, and expedition items. Empty Soda and Snack Machines gained a pulsing stock warning, with repair warnings taking priority when necessary.

Ronny gained a Contacts call sequence that could lead to a free package the following morning. That delivery contained the exclusive Ol'Money Washer, a slower machine distinct from the researched Money Washer. I also improved dialogue grammar, Money Washer explanations, Operation text scaling, journal cleanup, and interface visibility during conversations. Police and LBI visitors received an officer portrait, and additional confused and hypnotized emotes were animated.

The modular daily-event system began with Lost Wallet, Smelly Loiterer, and Abandoned Laundry. The wallet offered a decision between returning it and keeping the money, with rewards and consequences for happiness and suspicion. The loiterer wandered, used activities, reduced cleanliness, and could be removed. Abandoned orders left laundry for an owner who returned the following day. I expanded the animated customer pool and adjusted the loiterer's movement so wandering stayed central to the event.

Lost Wallet then grew into a returning-owner sequence with a matching appearance, physical handoff, reward, and saved progress. Sleeping Customer added someone who could occupy a washer until the player woke them. Health Inspector introduced an inspection route, violations, cleanliness results, fines, and a possible backroom inspection. Influencer Review evaluated the business through an actual laundry visit. By the end of this week, six gameplay events were available.

Crime began leaving evidence. Removing processed money, depositing criminal money in a Safe, and completing schemes could leave physical paper trails. A Trash Can and researched Paper Shredder offered different ways to remove that evidence and reduce Suspicion, and the shredder gained a one-shot animation. I moved money-laundering evidence and suspicion changes to the moment processed cash was removed, making the consequence match the player's action.

Ronny's Favors became modular. The existing friend-laundry request became the first favor, followed by No Questions Asked: a suitcase delivery with an advance, a later return, cooldowns, payment, and Mob Approval consequences. The suitcase also contained a hidden skeleton outcome. Service-order work included repaired bag pickup, an overflow position for abandoned bags, and customer hover information showing spending across laundry, services, shopping, entertainment, vending, and alien tips.

The cellphone interface replaced more of the old tab navigation. Operations and Contacts gained phone screens, with separate Schemes and Quests lists, Ronny's contact details, and active and completed Operation history. I moved favor and daily-event tracking into the phone and simplified the Scheme Desk around discovery and Keep/Trash decisions. Cheats remained available through Settings, and I corrected interactions between dialogue, phone screens, time controls, and the Open/Closed display.

The Services app brought Construction and advertising into the phone. Both laundromat and lair expansions moved under Construction. Flyers, Newspaper, Radio, and Television became purchasable campaigns with different costs, traffic bonuses, and durations. Campaigns started the next business day, could not stack, and recorded their spending in Metrics and daily reports. The advertising menu was simplified to short purchase buttons with details on hover.

A $250 Community Bulletin Board added five kinds of local sponsorship request, including contribution goals, expiration, cooldowns, sponsored states, community effects, newspaper entries, and spending records. Seven customer personalities changed patience, spills, shopping, and entertainment behavior, with names visible on hover and personalities preserved in saves. Customer waves also became staggered arrivals, with people entering one at a time instead of appearing as a single group.

The artwork received another substantial rotation pass: 66 new directional frames completed four-direction coverage for 30 purchasable shop objects. I kept existing front animations and broken-machine artwork while integrating directional washer and dryer sheets. Storefronts, benches, the Chemist Station, Research Desk, and Scheme Desk received perspective and footprint refinements so they fit the rest of the furniture more consistently.

I created a comprehensive Master Game Document to record the implemented systems and distinguish them from future plans. Additional work corrected package footprints, improved bag and icon handling, and documented the appliance rotation rules, giving the expanding project a more reliable reference for future development.

title: The Lair Becomes a Workplace
excerpt: Worker assignments, Ribs, counterfeit production, rats, outages, Puppet Master, ATMs, and Arc machines made this the busiest week yet.
body: Week 6: October 30–November 5, 2026, with development changes recorded through November 4. This week connected the lair's activities much more closely to the laundry business. I added staffed production, new uses for waste materials, another henchman, more disruptions, another major Operation, and a substantial round of placement and visual improvements.

Operation: A Safe Bet became the introductory scheme for tutorial players. Its short discovery and research steps led into purchasing and placing a Safe, then awarded the normal completion bonus. Tutorial players also received a guaranteed Lost Wallet on Day 2, connecting the lesson to a practical choice about returning or keeping someone else's money. Players who skipped the tutorial retained the normal random scheme and event flow. I fixed the tutorial's scheme button so it showed the short duration and could actually be used.

Completed Operations gained a paused clipboard report showing the Operation's purpose, actual outcome, permanent reward, and World Domination bonus. The Brain contributed a portrait and personal reaction, and completion audio played once. Reports queued behind other conversations, saved unread state, and resumed the previous game speed when dismissed. Later adjustments improved the centered COMPLETE heading, portrait border, and tan text panel, while redundant on-screen scheme notes were removed in favor of the phone.

Power Outage joined the daily-event pool. It darkened both rooms, interrupted normal electrical activity, and gave the player the option of waiting for recovery or calling an Electrician through Services. Follow-up work made customer machine cycles restart after power returned, paused service-order cycles, blocked loading machines while the power was out, stopped their animations, and added outage audio. The Electrician received a physical visit and repair sequence, dialogue, and saved progress.

Lair Rats became another recurring event, bringing the gameplay-event total to eight. Rats could move between rooms, harm public cleanliness, upset nearby customers, and cause an inspector to fail the business. Players could pick them up and relocate them, or buy a Rat Cage to store them. I corrected their directional animation, movement boundaries, carrying behavior, and furniture interactions. Filled cages could be moved but not sold. Later tuning reduced each event to one rat and made repeat rat events possible even when rats already existed.

The hidden Ratnest system connected lair clutter to infestation. Loose evidence, trash, plastic, lint, and spills contributed to the score, while removing or storing those materials lowered it. At a score of at least 10, the system made one 25% roll per day to spawn one rat, with the roll recorded in saves. Rat reactions gained a dedicated grossed-out emote, and I corrected impatient customers so they used their proper expression instead.

Dryers began producing collectible lint. Players could empty the traps, carry and combine piles, store material, or sell it through a working Safe. Full-trap indicators made maintenance visible. By the end of the week, Standard, Turbo, and Mega dryers had different lint capacities, and starting a cycle with a full trap added ten seconds. Lint on the public floor applied a cleanliness penalty that was restored correctly when the pile was removed.

The new Sewing Workshop turned lint into Ducci Wallets and Ducci Handbags. Players could select a recipe, collect the finished item, carry it around, and drop it on a working Safe to sell it. The workshop then gained a shared 20-item finished-goods inventory, individual withdrawal controls, and Make endlessly options. One selected recipe could repeat while materials, a worker, power, opening hours, and storage allowed it, pausing and resuming as conditions changed. A progress bar made active and paused work visible.

Plastic drops extended that production loop. Plastic could be combined, stored, discarded, or sold, and the workshop could turn it into Sike Basketball Shoes or Lordans. Finished shoes received random appearances that persisted in saves. Workshop raw-material storage was capped at 60 lint and 60 plastic, with overflow left in the player's hands. Ordinary vending litter also gained a clearer physical disposal loop: pick it up and carry it to a Trash Can.

I overhauled workstation staffing. Research Desks, Scheme Desks, and Sewing Workshops required the Brain or a henchman to make progress. Players could choose work before staffing the station, then assign a worker through a menu or by dropping the character onto it. Each station accepted one worker, assignments survived saving, and progress paused without an active worker. I improved access points, reduced the Brain's distance from stations, and made workers approach and face the correct operating side of rotated furniture.

Life Bringer, recipe 666, created a new use for Ronny's skeleton. Applying it introduced Ribs, complete with a revival conversation and a recruitment decision. Accepting brought him into the henchman system with duties, dragging, assignments, and persistent progress. His visible presence in the laundromat raised Suspicion, so I added a separate Allow Laundromat Access setting for each henchman. The Staff phone app provided profiles for Doyle, Carnegie, and Ribs, with portraits, known pay, backgrounds, and confirmed permanent termination.

Operation: Puppet Master connected community sponsorship to Mayor Knowscams. Lifetime Bulletin Board contributions counted toward the preparation goal, leading to a phone call, scheduled visits, a tour, the Brain Washer, and a ten-question leadership exam. Success produced a seat on the Small Business Committee, a contact entry, recurring visits, Happiness, and the Operation's domination reward. Failure supported later retries. The exam's questions remained temporary placeholder copy, but the progression and save support were implemented.

The Genie received four more working wishes: Never Clean Again, Unlimited Power, Stop Time, and Make Everything Bigger. These introduced timed spill prevention with extra litter, faster workstation production with increased breakdown risk, a temporary pause in the business clock while activity continued, and an extra row of floor space in both rooms. I also audited unfinished ideas and updated the documentation to distinguish approved additions, deferred work, and discarded concepts.

Contacts became more useful. Detective Lance gained a named contact entry after an inspection and a Community Safety Fund with once-per-business-day donations that reduced Suspicion. Anthony Bones gained expedition calls reporting his current destination and the days until his next package. I connected 19 completed treasure images, corrected their placement when packages opened, and made revealed treasures directly carryable and sellable by dropping them on a working Safe.

The ATM introduced withdrawals and a manually collected owner fee in the Bank app, with balance and lifetime totals. I fixed its reservation handling and limited each customer to one completed withdrawal per visit. The lair's Card Skimmer could link to an ATM and challenge the player to remember the latest customer's displayed PIN. A correct entry paid an additional share and raised Suspicion slightly; a wrong or stale entry raised it more sharply and disabled the ATM for the rest of the day.

Arc Washer and Arc Dryer research added another equipment tier. At $3,000 each, they combined Mega capacity of two loads with Turbo cycle speeds: 20 seconds for washing and 14 seconds for drying. I corrected their research-card placement and descriptions, added four-direction artwork, and refreshed the Sewing Workshop and Card Skimmer sprites. The Waiting Bench's front and back views were reduced to fit customer scale, and sleeping customers received a new looping, fading emote. A calendar now displayed January 1, Year 1 and advanced through months and years while preserving the internal day counter.

I rebuilt and refined the front facades for both rooms, extended the shared divider when only one side was expanded, and corrected gaps and pillar alignment. Front walls, corner pillars, and the exterior door gained a shared zoom fade plus wall-hiding options. Back and side walls ultimately remained opaque unless hidden. The exterior entrance received closed and entering-customer artwork while retaining its movement and routing behavior. Larger texture pages preserved the background's full resolution and its fine sidewalk lines.

Interaction fixes made loose objects and workers easier to select around furniture. Packages, treasure, evidence, crafted goods, and other portable items received foreground priority. Wallets stopped blocking customers, rats could no longer be trapped inside furniture, and held bags could be selected ahead of workstations. Ronny's package delivery received the correct large parcel artwork and waited for the player to talk to the Postal Worker. The mortgage report correctly advanced to Next Day after payment, with the phone visible above the dimmed report.

Other business fixes restored eligible Bulletin Board postings, improved Storefront purchase bubbles, removed unnecessary zero-value rows from daily reports, corrected advertising-menu argument errors, and refined completed-research feedback. The Brain gained four-direction rotation, reliable pickup, automatic workstation facing, and exemption from furniture attraction. Opened suitcases could be sold by dropping them on a Safe or disposed of in a Trash Can.

Finally, I addressed the brief jump and stutter associated with picking up objects. Pickup previews now update at the cursor immediately, nearby-item snapping avoids unnecessary collision checks, navigation compares stable obstacle layouts, and wall geometry is cached between relevant layout changes. Focused checks preserved placement and navigation behavior while reducing repeated work. The latest native builds compiled and started successfully; busy-game frame times and several new visual interactions still need direct in-game verification. Save migrations were added throughout the week to preserve existing progress as these systems expanded.
